title: Telemetry moderator for region fanout and fallback orchestration
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight telemetry mediator that synthesizes p50/p95 latency signals and a network-integrity score to drive region selection, tier routing, and automated fallback to compatible model variants. The mediator should be safe-by-default (no oscillations), explainable (reason codes for routing decisions), and efficient (compute <5% added latency in the decision path).

Problem statement: Current georouter uses simple percentile thresholds per POP and a separate circuit-breaker for link errors. We see two classes of failures: (1) transient jitter where p95 spikes briefly, causing thrashing between regions, and (2) partial degradation where latency is within thresholds but packet loss or TCP resets indicate poor link health. Both cases lead to visible customer retries and tail-latency regressions.

Scope: Design + implement mediator service and a small control-plane policy engine that emits ranked region lists with reason codes and selected fallback model variant when applicable. This work includes: ingest adapters for p50/p95 and packet-loss/conn-failure metrics, scoring function prototype, hysteresis and dampening knobs, integration with existing route dispatcher, end-to-end test harness, observability/alerting, and a rollout plan.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Mediator produces stable region ranking for synthetic workloads for 95% of injected spike experiments (no thrash).
- On degradations where network-health score < 0.6, mediator recommends fallback variant or cross-region failover with a documented reason code.
- E2E latency regression vs baseline <= 3% on nominal traffic after canary.
- New dashboards surface: per-request reason code, selected region, p50/p95 inputs, network-health score, and decision latency.

Design summary: 
1) Inputs: rolling-window p50 and p95 (30s, 5m), EWMA packet loss and connect-failure rate (1m), optional TCP RTO spikes.
2) Scoring: compute normalized z-like scores for p50 and p95 vs baseline distribution per region; combine with network-health penalty into a single region_score = w_lat * latency_score + w_net * (1 - net_health). Default weights w_lat=0.7, w_net=0.3.
3) Safety: implement hysteresis via decay timers and minimum-stable-window (default 60s) per promoted/demoted region. Add cooldown backoff exponential up to 15m to avoid oscillation.
4) Fallback variants: model-compatibility table maps primary variant -> lighter quantized/shorter-context variant. Mediator selects fallback when predicted cost/latency benefit > threshold and network_health < 0.6.
5) Explainability: attach reason tags (latency_p95_spike, net_loss_high, variant_fallback, stable_routing) to each decision.
6) Telemetry: emit decision traceid that ties to request logs and KV-cache usage to measure downstream impact.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Weighting latency vs network: prioritizing p95 avoids tail issues but may prefer distant regions with high variance; weights are configurable per customer tier.
- Complexity vs latency in decision path: we keep mediator asynchronous for non-blocking ranking refreshes; use short-lived cached rankings in the dispatcher to keep per-request latency low.

Rollout plan: 
- Step 1 (canary): read-only mode exposing recommendations to ops for 48h (observability check).
- Step 2: shadow routing for 1% traffic with canary region gating for 24h.
- Step 3: progressive enable for 10%, 30%, 100% with automatic rollback on SLO breach.

Open questions / next work: 
- Do we incorporate per-customer region affinities stored in user profile store? (PM flagged potential privacy surface)
- Calibration for w_lat/w_net per workload class (embedding vs chat) needs experimentation.

Docs & artifacts: design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atl/confluence/display/INF/Telemetry+Mediator+Design, decision matrix spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/fakesheet, prototype notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-mediator/blob/main/notebooks/score-proto.ipynb
